name: speech-input
title: Speech Input
description: A circular dictation button. Tapping it starts listening, turns it red with a stop square and sends out pulsing rings; tapping again ends the recording and hands the words to your text field.
use: A composer or email box should let people speak their message instead of typing it.
avoid: Needs browser speech support or a transcription callback; without either the button stays disabled and does nothing.
a11y: A label can be passed in but there is no default one or pressed state, so the recording toggle is silent to screen readers. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded card holding two lines of grey draft text, a small hint at the lower left and a round button at the lower right. The button is white with a dark microphone glyph, and red with a white square while recording.
behaves: Tapping starts listening: the button fills red, the glyph swaps to a stop square and three rings pulse outward on staggered delays. Tapping again returns it to white, and a spinner takes the glyph's place while the audio is being transcribed.
customise: The language, transcript callback and optional audio-recording fallback are props, and all button props pass through; ring colour and timings need a source edit.
weight: light: One button plus three CSS rings; nothing animates until recording starts.
demo: Draft email to Jordan about Thursday at 3pm and venue parking, with a hint line under it.
issues: No frame shows dictated words arriving in the field, so the main payoff is unproven in the clip.
The pulse rings are faint at this scale and mostly lost against the dark card.
polishWhy: Tidy standard icon button with a clear red listening state, but the demo shows little of the payoff.
